title: Downward Paths with Square Product
statement:
During a data-integrity audit, the servers of a data center form a rooted dependency tree with `n` servers numbered `0` to `n - 1`. The **root** server is `0`.

Each server `i` stores a positive integer `A[i]`, its integrity signature.

A **backup chain** is a path that starts at some server and ends at one of its descendants (possibly the same server), moving only along parent-to-child links. A backup chain is **stable** if the product of the signatures of all servers on it is a perfect square.

Count the stable backup chains. Chains are different when their (start, end) pairs differ; a single server counts as a chain of length one.

The tree is given as `n - 1` undirected edges; the direction (parent to child) is determined by the root `0`. The answer can exceed 32 bits.

The depth of the tree (number of servers on the longest root-to-leaf path) is at most 5000.
inputFormat:
The first line contains `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `A[0] ... A[n-1]`.
Each of the next `n - 1` lines contains two integers `u v`, an edge between servers `u` and `v` (0-indexed).
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the number of stable backup chains.
constraints: The edges form a tree; its depth when rooted at 0 is at most 5000

examples.explanation: The tree is the chain 0 - 1 - 2. Single servers 2, 3, 6 are not squares. Chain 0-1 has product 6, chain 1-2 has product 18, and chain 0-1-2 has product 36 = 6^2, a perfect square. So exactly one chain is stable.

The tree has edges 0-1, 0-2, 2-3 with values 1, 4, 2, 8. Stable chains: [0] (product 1), [1] (4), [0,1] (4), [2,3] (16) and [0,2,3] (16). The chains [2] (2), [3] (8), [0,2] (2) are not squares, so the answer is 5.

hints: A product is a perfect square exactly when every prime appears with an even exponent. Only 25 primes are below 100, so each signature can be reduced to a 25-bit parity mask.
Define prefix[v] as the XOR of the masks on the path root..v. The product on the chain from ancestor a down to v is a square iff prefix[v] == prefix[parent(a)] (use 0 for the parent of the root).

Run a DFS from the root and keep a hash map counting prefix masks of the current root path (including the empty prefix 0). At each node add the count of its own prefix mask to the answer, then insert it; remove it when leaving the node.
